steps: Efficiency is the ratio of useful work done by a machine to the work put into the machine.
Efficiency = (Useful work output / Work input) × 100%
The efficiency of a machine is always less than 100% because some of the input energy is wasted in overcoming friction and is transformed into heat and sound.
Therefore, the useful work output is always less than the work input.
items.finalAnswer: Efficiency is the percentage of the input work converted into useful output work; it is less than 100% because some energy is wasted, mainly due to friction.

items.figure: Water stored behind a dam → water flows down through a penstock → water turns a turbine → the turbine drives a generator → electrical energy.
steps: Water stored at a height behind a dam has gravitational potential energy.
When released, the water flows down and its potential energy changes into kinetic energy.
The moving water turns the blades of a turbine.
The turbine drives a generator, which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
Draw the blocks in this order, joining each block with an arrow: Reservoir (stored water) → Flowing water → Turbine → Generator → Electrical energy.
items.finalAnswer: The falling water turns a turbine, which drives a generator to produce electrical energy.

items.figure: Fossil fuel → boiler (water heated to steam) → steam turns a turbine → the turbine drives a generator → electrical energy.
steps: Fossil fuel is burned in a boiler to heat water.
The water changes into high-pressure steam.
The steam turns a turbine.
The turbine drives a generator, which converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
Draw the blocks in this order, joining each block with an arrow: Fossil fuel → Boiler (steam) → Turbine → Generator → Electrical energy.
items.finalAnswer: Burning fossil fuels produces steam that turns a turbine, which drives a generator to produce electrical energy.

steps: Given: F = 20 N, θ = 60°, s = 3 m
Required: Work done, W
Formula: W = Fs cos θ
Substitution: W = (20 N)(3 m) cos 60°
Working: W = 60 × 0.5 N m = 30 J
Result: W = 30 J
Given: F = 8 N, s = 5 m, W = 20 J
Required: Angle θ between the force and the direction of motion
Formula: W = Fs cos θ
Substitution: 20 J = (8 N)(5 m) cos θ
Working: cos θ = 20 / 40 = 0.5; therefore, θ = 60°
Result: θ = 60°
Given: m = 100 kg, h = 80 m, t = 25 s, g = 10 m/s²
Required: Power, P
Formula: P = Work done / time = mgh / t
Substitution: P = (100 kg)(10 m/s²)(80 m) / 25 s
Working: P = 80000 J / 25 s = 3200 W
Result: P = 3200 W
Given: m = 20 kg, u = 0 m/s, F = 40 N, t = 5 s
Required: Kinetic energy, KE
Formula: F = ma; v = u + at; KE = ½mv²
Substitution: a = 40 N / 20 kg = 2 m/s²; v = 0 m/s + (2 m/s²)(5 s)
Working: v = 10 m/s; KE = ½(20 kg)(10 m/s)² = 1000 J
Result: KE = 1000 J
Given: m = 160 g = 0.160 kg, h = 20 m, g = 10 m/s²
Required: Potential energy gained, PE
Formula: PE = mgh
Substitution: PE = (0.160 kg)(10 m/s²)(20 m)
Working: PE = 32 kg m²/s² = 32 J
Result: PE = 32 J
